draft_summary.title: Multi-spectral Observations of Lunar Occultations: I. Resolving The Dust Shell Around AFGL 5440
draft_summary.authors: Paul M. Harvey and Andrew Oldag
draft_summary.field_subfield: Astrophysics: Stellar Mass Loss / AGB Stars
draft_summary.type_of_paper: Observational Study with Radiative Transfer Modeling
draft_summary.executive_summary: This study presents high-speed, multi-spectral lunar occultation observations of the carbon-rich AGB star AFGL 5440, conducted over the 1–4µm wavelength range using the pMIRAS instrument. The primary goal was to resolve the spatial structure of the circumstellar dust shell, which had previously been inferred only from spectral energy distributions (SEDs). By fitting the observed diffraction fringes with radiative transfer models (DUSTY), the authors constrained the inner radius of the dust shell to a temperature of 950 K ± 50 K and an optical depth of 0.5 ± 0.1 at 5µm. The data strongly support a density gradient of ρ ∝ r⁻², consistent with radiatively driven hydrodynamic outflows. A significant finding is that models fitting the near-infrared occultation data and SED fail to reproduce the far-infrared (60µm) flux unless a substantial abundance of graphite is included or a significantly higher historical mass-loss rate is assumed. The study successfully separates the stellar photosphere (angular diameter ~3 mas) from the inner edge of the dust shell (angular radius ~11 mas), providing direct constraints on the recent dust mass-loss rate of approximately 6.5 × 10⁻⁸ M⊙/yr.

draft_summary.title: Gluon Radiation of an Expanding Color Skyrmion in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
draft_summary.executive_summary: This paper calculates the density of states and energy spectrum of gluon radiation emitted by an expanding color skyrmion within the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). Using a semiclassical approach applied to a nonlinear sigma model describing an ideal fluid, the author derives the nonabelian current for a time-dependent soliton solution. The study compares these results with existing literature on jet quenching and medium-induced radiation. The findings reveal a specific spectral pattern: a fast fall-off in the ultraviolet (UV) region, a smooth peak dominating the intermediate energy range, and a long tail in the infrared (IR). The IR behavior is characterized by a number density scaling as 1/sqrt(k), which differs from the 1/k scaling found in models assuming an infinitely large medium. The work suggests that the finite size of the soliton (R0) softens the IR behavior compared to infinite-medium approximations. Additionally, the study highlights a hierarchy between the characteristic momentum of the skyrmion (1/R0) and the typical frequency of medium-induced radiation (omega_C), implying distinct physical mechanisms at play. The results are presented as functions of a dimensionless parameter lambda, with numerical results provided for lambda values of 1/15, 2/15, and 1/5.

top_influential_citations.justification: This citation refers to the foundational review of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the hydrodynamic stage of its evolution, providing the physical context for the study of gluon radiation in this medium.

This citation introduces the concept of medium-induced gluon radiation in the context of final state partonic energy loss, which is the primary motivation for investigating radiation patterns in the QGP.

This citation discusses the role of gluon density saturation and strongly interacting gluonic atmospheres in the initial stage of thermalization, contrasting with the hydrodynamic approach taken in this paper.
This citation reports the discovery of single skyrmion solutions in color fluid, which serves as the specific soliton model used to calculate the nonabelian current in this study.
This citation provides the experimental evidence from RHIC experiments regarding the expanding nature of the fireball, justifying the use of a time-dependent expanding soliton solution.
